directAnswer: Pope Alexander IV was Rinaldo dei Conti di Segni, a nephew of Pope Gregory IX, who led the Church from 12 December 1254 until his death at Viterbo on 25 May 1261. He is remembered for canonizing St. Clare of Assisi, defending the mendicant friars at the University of Paris, uniting several hermit groups into the Augustinian friars, and continuing the papal struggle against the Hohenstaufen in southern Italy.

sections.h2: A Conti Cardinal and Friend of the Franciscans
paras: Rinaldo was born at Anagni, south of Rome, into the Conti di Segni family that had already given the Church Innocent III and Gregory IX. His uncle Gregory IX made him a cardinal, and he later became cardinal bishop of Ostia. For years he served as cardinal protector of the Franciscan Order, which gave him close knowledge of the friars and of the community of Poor Clares at San Damiano.

When Innocent IV died at Naples in December 1254, the cardinals gathered there chose Rinaldo within days. He took the name Alexander and inherited both his predecessor's unfinished war with the heirs of Emperor Frederick II and an unsettled Rome, where the city's senators and factions often made residence difficult. Much of his pontificate was spent at Anagni and Viterbo.

Clare of Assisi had died in August 1253, and Innocent IV opened the inquiry into her holiness. Alexander completed it, canonizing her at Anagni in 1255, only two years after her death. The bull of canonization praised her poverty and her life of enclosed prayer, and it set the Poor Clares firmly within the Church's official devotion.

His long connection with the Franciscans also shaped his decisions on their behalf. He confirmed privileges for the friars and supported their pastoral work in parishes and universities, even when local clergy objected.

sections.h2: Defending the Friars at Paris and Forming the Augustinians
paras: In the 1250s secular masters at the University of Paris, led by William of Saint-Amour, attacked the Dominicans and Franciscans who held teaching chairs there. William's treatise on the perils of the last times argued that the friars' way of life was dangerous. In 1256 Alexander condemned that work and ordered the university to readmit the mendicant masters, a decision that protected the place of teachers such as Thomas Aquinas and Bonaventure.

The same year he brought together several groups of Italian hermits into a single order under the Rule of St. Augustine, an event known as the Grand Union of 1256. The Order of Hermits of St. Augustine, later simply the Augustinian friars, traces its organized existence to that act. He also extended the authority of Dominican and Franciscan inquisitors in France, continuing measures his predecessors had begun against heresy there.

sections.h2: Manfred and the Kingdom of Sicily
paras: Politically, Alexander's reign was dominated by the question of who would rule the Kingdom of Sicily, which the popes regarded as a papal fief. He continued Innocent IV's plan to grant the crown to Edmund, son of King Henry III of England, but the English were unable to pay or send an army. Meanwhile Manfred, a son of Frederick II, consolidated control and had himself crowned king at Palermo in 1258.

Alexander excommunicated Manfred, but the papacy lacked the resources to remove him. The problem passed to his successors, who would turn to Charles of Anjou. Alexander died at Viterbo in May 1261 and was buried there.

keyFacts: Born Rinaldo dei Conti di Segni at Anagni; nephew of Pope Gregory IX
Elected at Naples in December 1254; reigned until 25 May 1261
Canonized St. Clare of Assisi in 1255
Condemned William of Saint-Amour's attack on the mendicant friars (1256)
Formed the Augustinian friars through the Grand Union of 1256
Died and was buried at Viterbo

faqs.question: Which saint did Pope Alexander IV canonize?
faqs.answer: He canonized St. Clare of Assisi in 1255 at Anagni, about two years after her death in 1253. The cause had been opened by his predecessor Innocent IV.

faqs.question: How did Alexander IV help the Dominicans and Franciscans?
faqs.answer: When secular masters at the University of Paris tried to push the friars out of teaching, he condemned William of Saint-Amour's treatise against them in 1256 and ordered the university to restore the mendicant masters to their chairs.

faqs.question: Why is Alexander IV important to the Augustinian friars?
faqs.answer: In 1256 he united several communities of Italian hermits into one order following the Rule of St. Augustine. This Grand Union is regarded as the formal beginning of the Order of Hermits of St. Augustine.
